blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Enterprise IT service desks process tens of thousands of internal
tickets per month, where the “customer” is an employee asking
internal IT for help with hardware, access, or software (not an
external consumer). HDI/MetricNet reports the North American
average cost per voice IT service-desk ticket at US$17.19, with
walk-up tickets averaging US$37.52 [ 1 ] . Routing happens under
an asymmetric cost structure. Sending a ticket to the correct queue
is nearly free. Sending it to a human triager is moderately
costly. Sending it to the wrong queue is much more
expensive once you account for handoff latency, double work, and
missed service levels. Accuracy or macro-F1 alone cannot represent
this asymmetry or indicate when to trust an automated decision [ 2 , 3 ] .

blocks.en:
Two trends make this gap more pressing. First, large language
models (LLMs) can be prompted as zero- or few-shot text classifiers [ 4 , 5 ] , potentially reducing the
need for task-specific training. Second, modern neural classifiers,
including LLMs, are known to be poorly calibrated. They often
produce high confidence values regardless of actual accuracy [ 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 ] . Together these trends raise a concrete
operational question: should a prompted LLM be allowed to
auto-route IT tickets, and if so, under what abstention policy?

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Selective prediction and abstention. The classical framework for rejecting uncertain inputs traces back
to Chow’s error-reject trade-off [ 3 ] . It has
been formalized for modern classifiers under the names selective
prediction [ 2 , 13 ] and
learning with abstention [ 14 ] ; a recent survey
organizes LLM abstention methods, benchmarks, and evaluation metrics [ 15 ] . The closest
line is learning to defer , where a classifier is trained
jointly with the option to pass an instance to a human expert [ 16 , 17 ] . Our training-free
confidence-threshold policy addresses the same route-or-defer action
space without joint training. We evaluate its decisions under an
explicit cost model following Elkan’s cost-sensitive formulation [ 10 ] .

agreement-across-predictors as a confidence signal inspired
by self-consistency [ 12 ] .

blocks.en:
The framework could be integrated into an IT service management
pipeline as a deferral layer, subject to operational validation. Here,
“readiness” remains conditional: an operator must estimate local costs,
reserve calibration data, freeze the policy, and monitor drift.
Defer-all is a warning under those inputs, not a permanent verdict
about a model family. The framework is agnostic to how the
underlying classifier was produced.

blocks.en:
Internal: label noise, prompt/output-budget sensitivity, and
remote-endpoint change remain possible despite temperature 0. The
LLMs saw names and at most three examples per class, not label
definitions or fine-tuning; the observed accuracy gap therefore
mixes model behavior with unequal taxonomy access. A definition-rich
prompt is an important future control, but rerunning changed
proprietary endpoints would not be directly comparable to the frozen
May 2026 outputs. External: generalization to private enterprise corpora is
not established, and the cost model is illustrative: real cost
parameters need to be estimated per organization. The post-hoc grid
broadens the tested ratios but does not validate them as realistic
for any service desk. All results use one
public corpus, and remote endpoints are snapshots rather than a
longitudinal test; we do not test temporal drift, cross-organization transfer, or input
distribution shift, and multi-corpus validation is future work. A
single stratified random split can also place near-duplicate or
template-like tickets in both train and test, which could favor the
lexical classifiers. We normalized ticket text and represented it

materially explain the classifier-versus-LLM gap.

mapping from category to downstream queue, and we assume deferred
tickets are ultimately routed correctly, modeling human triage only
as a fixed cost c triage c_{\mathrm{triage}} (triager error and variable

We compare score-based rejection, including margin and entropy, but

blocks.en: VII Conclusion
blocks.zh: 七. 结论

blocks.en:
We presented a reproducible empirical framework for asking whether
automatic ticket routing is cost-preferred under stated assumptions.
On one public corpus and primary illustrative ( 0 , 1 , 5 ) (0,1,5) costs, a
calibration-selected TF-IDF + LR policy reduces held-out modeled
cost by 38.1 %; in a post-hoc 16-setting cost analysis, frozen
calibration-selected policies beat both always-route and always-defer in 14
settings. The fixed break-even rule defers every ticket for
seven prompted LLM conditions and routes only 19/1,000 for Haiku
few-shot. Isotonic lowers ECE but generally does not improve
correctness ranking. The result is a scoped deployment warning, not
a universal ranking of model families. Separating prediction,
confidence, rejection, and cost makes each assumption auditable and
allows future datasets, prompts, learned deferral methods, and local
cost estimates to be evaluated under the same protocol.
